headline: A European Stock Trader’s Guide Ahead of the US Midterms
author: Levin Stamm and Matt Clinch

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- European equity investors are turning their attention to next week's US midterm elections, with the outcome potentially shaping the earnings outlook for a range of industries across the continent.
Most Read from Bloomberg

Policy in areas from defense spending and tariffs to drug pricing and research funding could shift depending on whether Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress. Currently, polls and prediction markets indicate a high likelihood that Republicans will lose control of the House of Representatives, while the outcome for the Senate is less certain.

"Midterms do matter for Europe, as European equities have substantial US revenue exposure," said Andrea Gabellone, head of global equities at KBC Securities. "A Democratic House and Senate give them greater scope for coordinated funding negotiations, especially in healthcare, clean energy and defense."
Here's a breakdown of what to watch around the Nov. 3 vote:

While Europe has few stocks that directly benefit from the AI investment boom relative to the US or Asia, a handful could face greater earnings uncertainty if Democrats gain more influence in Congress.
"The industry is responding to a political backdrop that is increasingly scrutinizing AI and data centers," Deutsche Bank AG analysts wrote in a report.

For European firms in the "picks and shovels" part of the US data-center buildout chain, a more stringent regulatory backdrop holds the potential for delays and setbacks to the construction boom. STMicroelectronics NV, Schneider Electric SE and Nokia Oyj are among the companies in the space with the highest exposure to the US.

Still, strategists at JPMorgan Chase & Co. including Dubravko Lakos-Bujas expect AI capex momentum to remain intact after the midterms and potentially even strengthen in 2027 and 2028. Companies will seek to meet AI demand and advance investment "before political risks intensify around the next presidential cycle," the team said in a note.

Stocks to watch: ASML Holding NV, ASM International NV, BE Semiconductor Industries NV, STMicroelectronics, Infineon Technologies AG, Nordic Semiconductor ASA, Nokia, OVH Groupe SA, Schneider Electric, Aixtron SE, ABB Ltd

Pharmaceutical companies stand to be among the biggest European beneficiaries of a "blue wave" that would see Democrats take the House and the Senate. Greater Democratic control of Congress could slow the White House's push for funding cuts and tighter oversight of research grants. The same is true for university and research funding, according to Oddo BHF strategist Thomas Zlowodzki.
If Democrats "were to succeed on these points in the budget negotiations, this would primarily support the purchase of laboratory equipment, reagents and consumables," Zlowodzki wrote in a note.

That would help healthcare stocks continue their recent outperformance against other parts of the market, facilitated by investors' preference for safer stocks amid rising yields and worries about government finances.

Still, Bloomberg Intelligence's Duane Wright highlighted that "European pharma companies will still face US policy uncertainty" even if the midterms were to produce a divided government and legislative gridlock.
Stocks to watch: Merck KGaA, Tecan Group AG, Sartorius AG
Utilities and Renewables

Opposition to renewable energy could ease if Democrats gain ground, according to Amundi strategists, potentially improving the sector's competitiveness with fossil fuels. The JPMorgan strategists say their blue-wave scenario would be encouraging for clean-energy stocks through greater support on appropriations, oversight and permitting. Citigroup Inc. analyst Martin Wilkie, meanwhile, cautioned that changes to Federal policy likely wouldn't have an impact before 2028.

Oddo BHF highlights European names including Engie SA and Iberdrola SA for their renewables exposure, as well as National Grid Plc for its role in powering the AI buildout. The London-listed utility, which generates 69% of its sales in the US, has previously received a $50 million Department of Energy grant toward a $140 million smart-grid project. More recently, it invested in a US company developing a natural gas-fired power plant for Microsoft Corp. in Texas.
Stocks to watch: Iberdrola, EDP Renewables SA, RWE AG, Engie, Orsted AS, Vestas Wind Systems AS
Construction and Materials

The election outcome isn't expected to fundamentally alter construction's regulatory framework. However, a strong Democratic showing could give the party more scope to influence policy through budget negotiations. Support for construction is broadly bipartisan, with the main differences centered on how projects are funded and around energy-efficiency renovations.

Oddo's Zlowodzki highlights Cie de Saint-Gobain SA and Heidelberg Materials AG, among others, with both generating roughly 20% of sales in the US. Saint-Gobain is exposed to building and renovation through its local plasterboard business, while Heidelberg Materials is more sensitive to local construction and infrastructure spending through its cement, aggregates, concrete and asphalt operations. Saint-Gobain and Heidelberg Materials have fallen 22% and 32%, respectively, year-to-date.

Meanwhile, the JPMorgan strategists said a "red wall scenario," that sees Republicans keep both the House and the Senate, would likely favor construction and building materials stocks, offering the most supportive incremental backdrop for the AI and infrastructure buildout through policy continuity.
Stocks to watch: Saint-Gobain, Heidelberg Materials, Sika AG
Oil and Gas

The crucial question for Europe's energy stocks is how the results alter the outlook for a peace deal in Iran, and ultimately commodity prices. Regardless of the outcome, there is speculation that President Donald Trump may order fresh strikes against Iran, potentially increasing the risk of renewed escalation. Elevated oil prices would spur profits for Europe's energy companies, which have already been a major driver of earnings growth this year.

Beyond geopolitics, Oddo flagged Technip Energies NV among the companies that stand to benefit from a Democratic victory, given its exposure to decarbonization engineering contracts, which would face fewer risks to funding. In contrast, TotalEnergies SE, as one of the largest liquefied natural gas exporters to the US, and Shell Plc, with major production sites in the Gulf of Mexico, would be more vulnerable to changes in the current policy framework.
Stocks to watch: Technip Energies, TotalEnergies, Shell

Democratic gains could add another headwind for European defense stocks. The elections could reset the Pentagon's fiscal 2027 budget toward 2026 levels and flatten spending growth through 2028, BI analysts Will Lee and George Ferguson wrote in a note. Oddo's Zlowodzki, meanwhile, said the risk "primarily relates to the future growth in US orders relative to expectations, not necessarily to existing contracts."

The boom in European defense stocks in 2025 was largely driven by expectations that the industry will help the continent disentangle itself from its US security guarantees. But since European governments have drawn up unprecedented spending packages, the sector has traded sideways as investors wait for those promises to become reality.
Stocks to watch: BAE Systems Plc, Leonardo SpA, Thales SA, Kongsberg Gruppen ASA
